# Design replication and accession occurrences

An accession correction changes what occupies a field position. It does not
move that position to another block or replication group. The following
contracts keep those two facts separate.

| Boundary | Design replication tag | Accession occurrence |
|---|---|---|
| Stock properties | `design_replicate` | `replicate` after field cutover |
| Operational layout cache | `design_rep_number` | `rep_number` |
| BrAPI standard replication level / v1 replicate | Design tag | Separate `additionalInfo.accessionOccurrence` |
| BrAPI explicit additional information | `designReplicate` | `accessionOccurrence` only when ready |
| Statistical matrix, existing 30/39 metadata columns | Existing `replicate` column | Not a blocking factor / not added as a trait |
| Updated mixed-model working input | `designReplicate` alias in the same metadata slot | Physical unit IDs identify individuals |
| Layout CSV/XLSX | Existing replication column is the design tag | Explicit `accession_occurrence` column |

## Recorded metadata and migration

`AddDesignReplicationStockprop` creates the new stock-property vocabulary and
`accession_occurrence_version` project-property vocabulary. Existing recorded
replication labels are captured before any counter is changed. This is a
snapshot of available records, not a reconstruction of a lost original design.
Do not infer Alpha/Lattice membership from accession counts or plot order.

A `design_replicate` row with a NULL value explicitly records missing metadata.
It differs from no snapshot row. Readers must not substitute an occurrence
counter for that recorded NULL. Zero is a valid recorded tag and is retained.
Same-field descendants inherit their plot's design tag; external sampling and
plate units retain the metadata of their own layout.

A whole field layout gets `accession_occurrence_version = 1` only in the same
transaction that normalizes its counters. Until then, a stored legacy replicate
must not be advertised as a modern occurrence counter. Public statistical
replication still resolves to the recorded design tag, or pre-cutover legacy
tag where no snapshot exists.

## Correction and creation

Before a field accession correction, preserve all design tags in the trial.
For the proposed final accession assignment, number every accession's planned
positions from 1 through N by numeric plot number, then stock ID. Only changed
values are written. Normalize all trial accessions on a membership change so
legacy group labels cannot remain mixed with occurrence counters. Same-trial
plants, subplots and samples receive the plot's occurrence; external layouts
keep their own local fields. A repeated correction is idempotent.

Check plots, rejected plots and unsown planned positions retain their places in
this numbering. These labels are not counts of eligible measurements. Analysis
eligibility and observation counts remain separate.

A pure status change or no-op does not renumber a layout. Native full-layout
creation uses an internal forced-normalization option after all positions are
stored. Genotyping wells and aggregated analysis units are not field-plot
occurrence domains.

Plot-name templates use the operational occurrence label. Recorded block and
design tags remain available separately. Preview digests cover those tags and
snapshot state, so a concurrent design-metadata edit invalidates an old preview.

## Model and API rules

The standard BrAPI replication hierarchy remains a recorded position/group tag.
An unchanged GET/PUT round trip preserves both concepts. Explicit design-tag
edits use the normal target-project permissions, update same-field descendants
and caches, and retain a NULL snapshot when cleared. Conflicting aliases fail;
the derived occurrence extension cannot silently overwrite a design tag.

Analytical producers resolve the design tag before filling their existing
`replicate` metadata slot. This preserves the established 30/39-column schemas
and trait offsets. Rich records also carry named design/counter/presence fields;
old cached JSON is enriched from live stored metadata. Models must not extract a
blocking effect from the operational counter.

Study design determines whether a recorded tag is a factor. CRD has no blocking
factor; RCBD uses its actual block; incomplete-block designs require the recorded
replication/block nesting. Missing, ambiguous or unsupported scientific metadata
must produce an explicit diagnostic, not invented groups or residual variance.
Repeated-measure individual identity uses observation-unit IDs, not a product of
germplasm name and a replication group.

## Acceptance

Verify old and new field layouts, all native/BrAPI correction entry points,
preview/apply/retry, noncontiguous tags, zero/NULL, swaps and over-replication,
children/external studies, concurrent edits, cache/export agreement and actual
native Alpha/Lattice generators. Qualify actual model inputs and numeric outputs,
including CRD dispatch and unsupported-estimator diagnostics. A green subset is
not completion while another affected path remains unexplained or unverified.

## Pooled samples and analytical cache identity

A pooled sample can have several physical plot sources, so its occurrence is
unknown even if those sources happen to have equal occurrence labels. Its
recorded group is known only when every source belongs to the same field context
and has the same recorded tag. Equal text across different fields is not one
group.

The current unit, BrAPI and phenotype contracts associate one unit with one
germplasm. A correction that would give a pooled sample divergent final source
identities is refused atomically: otherwise one measurement would appear under
multiple germplasms and could also break the materialized view's unique-unit
index. Review sample provenance instead of inventing an identity. A coherent
atomic correction of all its sources is allowed, including authorized BrAPI
batches across studies; no intermediate mixed identity is published.

A stale analytical cache must not join an old germplasm identity with a live new
occurrence. Materialized searches validate relevant live identities before
cached accession filtering and pagination. An outdated or ambiguous identity
requires a refresh/correction before emitting an analytical matrix or training
file; it is never silently dropped or reassigned.

Field descendants inherit their physical plot block, resolved from every source
plot in the same field context. Unanimous exact tags are known; conflicting,
missing or cross-field contexts remain unknown. This also retains the established
single-parent semantics for legacy tissues without their own block property.
Independent sampling and plate layouts keep their local block metadata. The raw
stored property remains inspectable; no historical block is reconstructed.

A field child counter is resolved through exactly one plot source. Pooled,
orphan and cross-field units do not advertise a local legacy label as a field
occurrence. The stored replicate remains separately inspectable and is what the
normalization planner compares when repairing missing or stale descendant rows.

`IncludeTissueSamplesInPhenotypeMatview` extends the existing derived-table
relationship predicate to include `tissue_sample_of`; previously refreshed tissue
observations could be absent from the supported tissue phenotype matrix. It
retains query columns and rebuilds derived data transactionally with the original
owner, privileges and indexes. Raw records remain unchanged. The ordinary
Dataset::File level choices are not expanded by this correction.

Curators may correct a recorded accession through BrAPI after measurements exist,
using the same service contract as the confirmed planting-file workflow. The
measurements and their IDs stay with the physical unit, and API status warnings
explain the changed attribution/design and need to rerun analyses. Ordinary
editors retain the existing measured-layout restrictions.

Seedlot reassignment locks the old and new lots in canonical order before the
planting transaction changes. Cached seed count and weight are then recalculated
together from one fresh transaction list under the same lock; cached per-object
transactions cannot overwrite another study's committed inventory changes.

## Native random-regression variance report by time

The native F90 trajectory report uses the actual fitted covariance model. With
basis vector `b(t)`, coefficient covariance matrices `QG` and `QPE`, genotype
kernel `K`, physical-unit kernel `L` and fitted log-residual coefficients `gamma`,
the marginal variances on genotype `i`, physical unit `j`, at time `t` are
`K[i,i] * b(t)' QG b(t)`, `L[j,j] * b(t)' QPE b(t)` and
`exp(b(t)' gamma)`. Keep the full matrices and their covariance cross-terms.
The printed native `SE for R` is a diagnostic standard error; it is never a
residual variance, time-specific uncertainty estimate or ratio denominator.
Fixed-covariance BLUP uses declared matrices and labels them supplied; AIREML
uses the validated final estimates and labels them estimated.

Report the genetic share of adjusted individual-observation variance. The
summary curve is the ratio of average marginal components over a fixed set of
fitted physical units, with equal per-unit weights archived with their IDs.
Keep the individual values/range, numeric time, DAP/GDD unit, actual basis,
kernel provenance and scale. Missing dates do not silently change the reference
population. Rescaling a kernel and inversely rescaling its coefficient covariance
must leave every projected marginal component and share unchanged.

Interpretation follows the biological model. Additive marker effects produce an
explicitly labelled additive/model share; independent genotypic effects may
represent broad-sense variation only when that interpretation is declared.
Phenotype-derived or unknown kernels do not justify an unqualified heritability
label. Invalid covariance kernels or unidentifiable/nonconverged fits produce a
named diagnostic. Do not change their estimator to manufacture a plausible H2.

This report does not estimate genotype-mean selection reliability. That metric
requires the actual averaging weights and prediction-error covariance of
contrasts; neither occurrence counters nor a maximum replication label provide
it. Preserve existing historical summary JSON, clearly identifying old native
coefficient-ratio results as legacy/unverified. Version the corrected report and
label across-simulation standard deviations separately from estimation SE.

Scientific basis: [Salimiyekta et al. (2021), equations 9–12](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8697866/)
and [Schmidt et al. (2019), individual versus entry-mean interpretation](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6707473/).

Native F90 input explicitly declares its missing-observation code. Actual numeric
zero is measured data. Only absent observations or held-out CV values use the
reserved code, and a real measurement colliding with that code is refused with
a diagnostic. Missing-input rows do not contribute placeholder fitted values,
residuals or error sums on readback. This coding rule does not change categorical
zero labels, pedigree identifiers or the statistical model.

Original native F90 output is a finite-precision numerical interface. A successful
exit alone does not establish a valid supplied kernel: the retained original
backend can silently use a partial generalized inverse for a numerically singular
kernel. Require the documented relative numerical-rank contract and report a
named unsupported-kernel diagnostic; never silently repair the supplied kernel.

AIREML text covariance entries can round a positive fitted matrix into an
apparently indefinite matrix. Preserve raw covariance/eigensystem text and its
decimal representation bounds. Use a reported spectral representation only when
nonnegative eigenvalues, orthogonality and covariance-entry consistency are
validated against the propagated printed precision. Label that readback source
and uncertainty explicitly. This is numerical output representation, not a new
fit, kernel repair, confidence interval or claim of unavailable full precision.

Explicit layout/Field Book `selected_columns` requests retain exactly the
requested metadata columns. Selecting `rep_number` does not silently insert an
extra occurrence column. Rich native defaults/UI can select both independently;
the separate `accession_occurrence` option is visible and removable. Existing
fixed-width custom layouts remain compatible. Plot eligibility/status policy
continues to apply independently of column selection.

A native variance JSON archive is successful only after a real readable file and
its digest exist. If archival fails after summary persistence, return a controlled
error with the saved protocol ID and saved-summary state. Retain the source JSON
and stored result; never present a nonexistent archive path as success.
